newsitem.title: USA: Dow snaps 2-day winning streak, techs manage gains.
newsitem.headline: Dow snaps 2-day winning streak, techs manage gains.

text.p: U.S. blue chip stocks closed lower on Wednesday as worries about the outlook for long-term interest rates caused investors to take profits after two straight record-breaking sessions on Wall Street.
But technology and small-cap stocks finished higher as investors remained attracted to their growth prospects.

"For the last few days, people thought rates were not going to rise, but they were ignoring the rise in rates since the Fed opted not to move," said Michael Metz, chief investment officer at Oppenheimer & Co.
The yield on the benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond has moved above seven percent since Federal Reserve policy-makers decided to make no change at a meeting earlier this month.
On Wednesday, the Dow Jones industrial average shed 26 points, or 0.35 percent, to close unofficially at 7357, after record high closes in the previous two sessions.

The session was marked by volatility, with the index sliding at the opening and later reversing course to make a timid move into positive territory. A round of brisk selling sent the Dow sharply lower, triggering curbs on the New York Stock Exchange, but the average again turned around.

The losses were largely limited to blue-chip stocks. In the broader market, technology issues again turned in a chart-busting performance, boosted by gains in networking stocks. The Nasdaq Commposite closed up one to 1410, and the Russell 2000 Index of smaller stocks rose one to 378.

"A lot of portfolio managers are peeling back their blue-chip holdings a little, because they have run very far, very fast," said Metz, adding that many are moving the money into small-capitalization stocks.

"Many small stocks were so depressed earlier that they have plenty of room to grow. Large-cap issues have some growth, too, but some of the more popular stocks are getting very pricey," said Peggy Farley, president of Amas Securities Inc.
The 30-year U.S. Treasury bond was unchanged late in the day, with the yield at 7.03 percent.

Some market analysts pointed out that it was the second session that stocks and bonds took different directions. At one point late in the session, blue chips swooned and moved to session lows, while long bond prices were slightly higher.
Growing optimism about sales and earnings in the computer networking sector sent those stocks soaring again, pushing the Nasdaq to its third record straight close.
3Com Corp jumped 4-3/8 to 51-1/8, adding to steady gains made since an April low of 26-3/4. U.S. Robotics Corp surged 7-3/4 to 88-1/2, and FORE Systems Inc rose 1-7/8 to 16-5/8.
Shares of HFS Inc and CUC International Inc both fell in heavy trading a day after they said they would combine in an $11 billion stock-swap merger.
HFS, whose brands include Ramada Inn and Century 21 Real Estate, shed four to close at 54-1/2, and Stamford, Connecticut-based CUC fell 2-3/4 to 23-1/4 on the NYSE.

Nike Inc shares jumped for a second straight session amid speculation that billionaire Warren Buffett favors the sporting goods company as an investment. Nike Class B stock rose 3-5/8 to 63-5/8 on the NYSE, where it was among the most active issues on volume of more than 4.47 million shares.
International Business Machines Corp rose 1/2 to 89-7/8 on the NYSE after a two-for-one stock split.
Charles Schwab Corp rose 2-7/8 to 38-3/4 after the stock was added to the Standard & Poor's 500, allowing the issue to benefit from assets allocated by mutual funds that track that index.
Breadth was positive, with advancers outpacing decliners 1,310 to 1,150 on the NYSE. Volume on the Big Board was 487.2 million.
The Dow Jones industrial average fell 26.18 to close officially at 7357.23. The S&P 500 fell 2.50 to 847.21.
The Nasdaq officially closed up 0.97 to 1410.18.
((-- Wall Street desk, 212-859-1881))
